image_description: A close-up portrait of a person with short reddish-brown hair and a plaid shirt. The subject has two adhesive bandages applied to their face: one on the forehead and one on the upper lip/philtrum area. The background is a smooth, neutral gray gradient.

The bandage on the forehead exhibits severe geometric distortion; it is not a clean rectangle but rather a warped, irregular polygon with uneven edges that do not follow a logical rectangular shape.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The geometry of the forehead bandage is nonsensical. It twists and warps in a way that defies the physical properties of a rigid-backed adhesive strip. The edges bleed into the skin, indicating a failure to maintain object boundary integrity.

The bandage on the lip lacks distinct edges and texture. It looks like a smudge of paint rather than a physical object stuck to the skin. The interaction with the lip contour is physically implausible.

There is noticeable edge bleeding where the bandages meet the skin. Instead of a sharp shadow or highlight indicating thickness/adhesion, the pixels blend, suggesting the generator struggled with the occlusion boundary.
